questions.stem: The diagram isolates the distal interphalangeal joints of digits 2–5. Which diagnoses are marked at this location? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the DIP-predominant distribution shared by osteoarthritis, erosive osteoarthritis, and psoriatic arthritis in this diagram.
questions.explanation: In the supplied distribution diagram, the DIP row is marked for osteoarthritis, erosive osteoarthritis, and psoriatic arthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis is shown with a more MCP/PIP and wrist-centered pattern, while pyrophosphate arthropathy and gout are marked elsewhere. This is a diagram-reading exercise, not a complete diagnostic rule.

questions.stem: The highlighted zone is the proximal interphalangeal joint row of digits 2–5. Which diagnoses are represented here? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Separate the PIP involvement shown across degenerative, inflammatory, and psoriatic patterns.
questions.explanation: The diagram marks the PIP row for osteoarthritis, erosive osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis. The important contrast is that rheumatoid arthritis is not a DIP-predominant pattern in this teaching diagram, whereas psoriatic arthritis can involve both DIP and PIP joints.

questions.stem: A single target is placed over the thumb interphalangeal joint. Which diagnoses have a marked thumb IP location in the source diagram? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Use the thumb IP marker as a distribution clue rather than assuming all thumb findings are first-CMC disease.
questions.explanation: The supplied diagram places a blue marker at the thumb IP joint for osteoarthritis, erosive osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis. Pyrophosphate arthropathy and gout are represented at the thumb MCP rather than this IP target.

questions.stem: The target is the metacarpophalangeal row of digits 2–5. Which diagnoses are marked at these MCP joints? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Identify the MCP-centered overlap of rheumatoid arthritis, pyrophosphate arthropathy, and gout in the source diagram.
questions.explanation: The MCP row is marked for rheumatoid arthritis, pyrophosphate arthropathy, and gout. Osteoarthritis and erosive osteoarthritis are shown with interphalangeal and thumb-base emphasis, while psoriatic arthritis is not marked at this MCP row in the supplied diagram.

questions.stem: The target is the thumb MCP joint. Which diagnoses are marked at this specific thumb location? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish thumb MCP involvement from thumb IP and first-CMC involvement.
questions.explanation: In the source diagram, rheumatoid arthritis, pyrophosphate arthropathy, and gout each have a thumb MCP marker. The osteoarthritis-family markers are placed at the thumb IP and thumb base instead.

questions.stem: The target is the first carpometacarpal (thumb-base) joint. Which diagnoses are marked here? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Recognize first-CMC emphasis in osteoarthritis and erosive osteoarthritis.
questions.explanation: The first-CMC target is marked for osteoarthritis and erosive osteoarthritis in the supplied diagrams. The inflammatory and crystal arthropathy markers in this set are concentrated at MCP, wrist, or other carpal locations.

questions.stem: The target is the triscaphe (scaphotrapezial-trapezoid, STT) region. Which diagnoses are marked at this wrist-base location? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Map the wrist-base degenerative markers to osteoarthritis-family patterns.
questions.explanation: The diagram marks the triscaphe/STT region for osteoarthritis and erosive osteoarthritis. Read the target as the joint distribution shown by the source, not as an attempt to label every possible cause of STT pain.

questions.stem: The target sits over the radiocarpal wrist. Which diagnoses have a marked radiocarpal distribution in the source diagram? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Recognize wrist-centered patterns and their overlap across inflammatory and crystal arthropathies.
questions.explanation: The radiocarpal wrist is marked for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and pyrophosphate arthropathy in the supplied diagram. Gout is marked at MCP and thumb MCP locations, while the osteoarthritis-family markers emphasize distal and thumb-base joints.

questions.stem: The target is the distal radioulnar–ulnar wrist region. Which diagnoses are marked at this location? Select all that apply.
questions.learningObjective: Identify the ulnar-wrist overlap shown for rheumatoid and pyrophosphate arthropathy.
questions.explanation: The lower ulnar-wrist target is marked for rheumatoid arthritis and pyrophosphate arthropathy in the source diagram. This focused target helps separate the wrist distribution from gout's marked MCP pattern.
